The scorer reads a page as one flat string and hands it to analyze(text, options). Inside, tokenize() splits the string into runs, makeKey() lowercases each run, and NGram.prototype.add() counts every context up to order 4. The defaults live in DEFAULT_SETTINGS: intensity 50, basis "auto", minTokens 80, and a blend weight that slides from 0.55 to 0.08 between 400 and 6000 tokens.

When the page has fewer than 600 tokens, the basis is surprisal; at 600 or more it becomes gain. The raw score is -Math.log2(pMix) for surprisal, and -Math.log2(pUni) + Math.log2(pMix) for gain. The result goes through smooth(), percentileRank() and toLevels(), which return an Int8Array with one level per token, from -2 to 2.

To compare the port with upstream, run node --experimental-strip-types scripts/skim-parity.mjs --upstream ~/src/skimgram. The script stages src/core/tokenizer.ts, ngram.ts, normalize.ts, scorer.ts and builtin.ts in a temporary directory, rewrites their imports, and calls analyze() on every file in tests/fixtures/skim. A token counts as a mismatch when its key, kind, offsets, level or score differs by more than 1e-9.

Names matter here: sd_skim_emph and sd-skim-emph are different keys, while MAX_CHARS, GAIN_MIN_TOKENS and MIN_SPREAD_BITS are constants. The localStorage keys are sd-read-mode, sd-read-last, sd-skim-intensity and sd-skim-basis. The CSS hooks are html[data-sd-skim~="dim"], .sd-sk[data-sk="-2"] and .sd-sk[data-sk="2"]. A path such as assets/skim-surprise.html or a flag such as --freq-dir counts as one token each, or several, depending on its hyphens.

Version strings like v1.2.3 and 4ebb78a are numbers or words depending on the letters inside them. A hash such as 4ebb78a becomes a word because it has letters, but 20261017 stays a number. Hyphenated terms like state-of-the-art, run-time and well-known keep their hyphens; a trailing hyphen- is dropped. Apostrophes work too: it's, don't and the programmers' habits.

None of this needs a network. The fixtures are plain text files, the goldens are JSON, and the check runs in about a second with node 22 or later. If a constant changes in the port, the golden run fails on the first token that moves; if upstream changes, regenerate the goldens with --write-golden and read the diff before committing.

A short checklist for a release: bump package.json to 0.1.2, run npm test, tag v0.1.2, push origin main, and attach dist/skimgram-0.1.2.zip. Then update docs/CHANGELOG.md, open issue #118 for the follow-up, and ping @maintainers in the channel. On the build host, set NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 before running vite build, because the userscript bundle inlines both word lists. The EN_WORDS string holds 3000 entries and CJK_CHARS holds 2000, so the two together stay near 28 KB.
